context.objective: Document how we carry out European Distribution Execution, the controls and what needs confirmation.

turns.text: Thanks for sharing. Give me a moment to digest the file. Then I’ll follow up with a question.
The table in “F09 FA-18C scanned pages.pdf” sets actions at T+7, T+8 and T+15 but does not define T. What event starts that timeline in the process described?

T is the date the client notifies us of the distribution. I do not know whether the T plus n days are business or calendar days, that has never been confirmed. On T the preparer opens the event: records T, the entity, the amount, the purpose and the expected payment date, sets up the schedule through T+15, identifies the preparer, reviewer and contacts, and opens the European distribution checklist. By T+3 the preparer with Fund Accounting drafts each investor's gross amount, any withholding and net payment, checks the investor totals agree with the approved fund-level distribution, and shares the draft with the client. The client comments by T+4, and by T+5 the preparer and reviewer update the calculations and allocations and prepare the distribution notices, repeating the affected checks. Then we run Exiger sanctions screening and check the CDD status of every payee; any blocked investor is marked, their payment is withheld and follow-ups are scheduled straight away for 30, 60 and 90 days. At T+6 we send the final calculation details and draft notices to the client, and the client approves the notices in writing at T+7.
How does the client’s distribution notification reach the preparer?

I do not know the exact channel, it is not fixed anywhere that I know of; the client notifies us and the preparer checks that T matches the date of that notification. For the rest: at T+8 the notices go out through the investor portal or by email, done by us or Investor Services, the exact role is not defined, and we keep the delivery record. If the client approval is missing at T+7 we do not send notices at T+8 and everything stops until it is resolved. Between T+8 and T+15 Fund Accounting and Treasury confirm cash is available now and through T+15, and the payments are prepared with the callback check, funding and dual approval, leaving out anyone who is CDD blocked. If funds are insufficient we hold the payment and escalate; I do not know who makes that decision. Payments are released at T+15 only to cleared investors; who actually releases, client or us, is not confirmed. Shortening the T+15 wait needs written approval from the Head of the applicable jurisdiction. From one day after the due date we report payment status and returned payments to the client until each item is resolved, returned payments are investigated, and blocked investors are followed up at 30, 60 and 90 days. If CDD clears we update the status and pay through the approved checks. If still blocked after 90 days we escalate, but the next step is not defined. Finally the preparer and reviewer file all records in the digital binder, initial the checklist and close the event, with open blocked or returned items tracked separately and not marked closed.
Outside a specific client distribution notification, how often does this work normally arise?

By T+3 the preparer and Fund Accounting draft each investor's gross amount, withholding and net payment, check investor totals against the approved fund-level distribution and share the draft with the client. The client comments by T+4.

Payments are released at T+15 only to cleared investors; whether the client or the team releases them is unconfirmed. A shorter wait requires written approval from the Head of the applicable jurisdiction.
